questions.explain: Triggers: history tokens exceeding ~70% of the history budget (summarize oldest 50%), session close (archival summary), and explicit checkpoints for long-running agent tasks.
options: Every 100 messages regardless of budget
Budget pressure at ~70% of history budget, session close, and explicit agent checkpoints
Only when the user asks for a summary
Once per day on a fixed schedule

questions.explain: from_seq/to_seq records exactly which turns a summary replaces; the loader's NOT EXISTS anti-join guarantees a summary and its covered turns never appear together — no gaps or overlaps.
options: Summaries are stored without any range information
from_seq/to_seq ranges plus a NOT EXISTS anti-join in the loader
Deleting summarized turns immediately
Relying on timestamps alone
questions.q: How does history assembly splice summaries and verbatim turns without gaps or double-counting?

questions.explain: The contract: preserve decisions, commitments, entities, identifiers, open questions; target ~15% compression ratio; write third-person dense style for machine consumption using a cheap model, since quality plateaus quickly.
options: Preserve decisions, entities, and open items at ~15% compression in dense third-person style, written by a cheap model
Write literary prose summaries with a frontier model
Summarize to a fixed 5 sentences regardless of length
Optimize summaries for human reading pleasure

questions.explain: When summaries accumulate, level-1 summaries roll up level-0 summaries via parent_summary_id; two levels handle essentially every real conversation — three levels means the conversation should have been split.
options: Summaries can never be summarized
Recursive summarization via parent_summary_id and summary_level; two levels handle nearly everything
Delete old summaries when they accumulate
Store all summaries in a separate database
questions.q: How does recursive summarization handle very long conversations?

questions.explain: An LLM judge compares answers from full history vs. summarized history monthly; if equivalence drops below ~90%, the compression ratio is too aggressive or the prompt needs reinforcing — it also catches prompt drift.
options: Human review of every summary
No validation is needed
Monthly LLM-judge comparison of full-history vs. summarized-history answers, threshold ~90%
Comparing summary length to original length
